# Patientdesk.ai Raises $3.8 Million to Expand AI-Powered Dental Practice Operations Platform

 VC Tavern August 24, 2026 

Patientdesk.ai has raised $3.8 million in total funding to accelerate the development of its artificial intelligence platform for dental practices, expanding its mission to automate front-office and back-office operations across the healthcare sector. The San Francisco-based startup plans to use the capital to enhance its AI-powered patient coordination platform, deepen integrations with practice management systems, and broaden its suite of administrative tools beyond appointment scheduling into insurance verification, payments, and care coordination.

The funding includes a previously announced $1 million pre-seed round led by Y Combinator with participation from E2VC. Since that financing, Patientdesk.ai has continued raising additional capital, bringing its total funding to $3.8 million as the company scales its operations following strong customer adoption.

Founded by Oncel Ozgul, Emre Kaplaner, and Fikri San Koktas, Patientdesk.ai was created after the founders spent years working closely with dental clinics and observing the operational challenges faced by front-desk teams. They found that dental offices routinely struggled with unanswered phone calls, manual appointment scheduling, insurance verification delays, payment collection, and fragmented administrative workflows. These inefficiencies often resulted in missed revenue opportunities and increased workloads for practice staff.

To address these challenges, Patientdesk.ai developed an AI-native operating system specifically designed for dental practice administration. Rather than functioning solely as an AI receptionist, the platform manages multiple operational workflows, including answering inbound phone calls, qualifying prospective patients, booking appointments directly into practice management systems, verifying insurance eligibility during conversations, collecting payments, and sending automated reminders. The company aims to provide continuous front-desk coverage while reducing administrative burdens on healthcare providers.

Unlike general-purpose conversational AI tools, Patientdesk.ai focuses exclusively on dental workflows. Its platform integrates with existing practice management software, enabling clinics to automate complex administrative processes without replacing existing operational systems. According to the company, its AI agents understand patient context, insurance information, appointment availability, and payment requirements, allowing them to perform tasks traditionally handled by human receptionists.

The company has reported rapid commercial traction since launching its platform. Patientdesk.ai says its technology is deployed across more than 60 dental clinics operating in the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom. During the period following its pre-seed financing, the company also reported significant growth in monthly recurring revenue while continuing to expand relationships with multi-location dental organizations.

The newly raised capital will be used to strengthen engineering capabilities, expand AI infrastructure, and introduce additional healthcare automation features. Patientdesk.ai plans to broaden its product beyond appointment scheduling by enhancing insurance verification, claims management, patient communications, and revenue cycle workflows. The company also intends to deepen integrations with leading practice management platforms used throughout the dental industry.

Artificial intelligence has become an increasingly important technology for healthcare administration as providers seek to reduce operational costs while improving patient experience. Administrative work accounts for a significant share of healthcare spending, with scheduling, insurance processing, billing, and patient communication often requiring substantial manual effort. AI-powered workflow automation has emerged as one approach to improving efficiency while enabling staff to focus more on patient care.

Investor support from Y Combinator and E2VC reflects growing venture capital interest in vertical AI companies building software tailored to specific industries rather than developing broad consumer applications. Dental practices represent a particularly attractive market because they combine high patient communication volumes with complex scheduling, insurance, and payment workflows that can benefit from automation.

Following its participation in Y Combinator’s Winter 2026 accelerator program, Patientdesk.ai has continued expanding both its customer base and product capabilities. The company believes its long-term opportunity extends beyond dentistry into broader healthcare administration, where many providers continue to rely on labor-intensive front-office processes that have changed little over the past decade.

With fresh funding led by Y Combinator and participation from E2VC, Patientdesk.ai is positioned to accelerate development of its AI-native operating system for healthcare providers. As demand grows for intelligent automation across medical practices, the company aims to help clinics improve operational efficiency, increase patient access, and modernize administrative workflows through artificial intelligence while enabling healthcare professionals to devote more attention to delivering patient care.

Patientdesk.ai: AI Native Operating System for Dental Clinics

See original launch post

TL;DR: Patientdesk handles inbound and outbound calls, scheduling, live insurance verification, claims submission, and billing for dental clinics — all in one system. We grew from $17K to $50K MRR in 8 weeks and have driven $1.8M in incremental revenue for our customers. https://youtu.be/1liipoEyTuk

👋 Hi, we're Oncel, Şan, and Emre.

We've been best friends since 2016. All three of us ranked #1 nationwide out of 1.2 million students on the Turkish national exam, ended up in the same high school dorm room, and have been working together ever since. Before Patientdesk, we ran a dental marketing agency and our own call center for two years. We didn't find this problem. It found us.

🔴 The problem

The US dental industry processes $189 billion in services annually across 135,000 clinic locations. Yet the average practice runs on five disconnected tools that don't talk to each other. The consequences are severe:

- 15% of insurance claims are denied, 80% of those denials are preventable
- 65% of denied claims are never resubmitted
- Front desk staff spend up to 20 hours per week on manual insurance verification alone

Every time data moves between tools, a human moves it manually. A wrong code, a missing attachment, a verification that never made it to the claim. The clinic doesn't get paid. This is not a staffing problem. It's a coordination problem. And you can't fix a coordination problem by adding more tools.

✅ What we built

Patientdesk is the AI-native operating system for dental practices. We started with the front office and we're building toward owning the entire stack.

Today we handle:

- Inbound and outbound calls — 24/7 coverage, no missed calls, no voicemails
- Scheduling — books directly into the practice management software
- Live insurance verification — we are the first system to verify insurance during the booking call, in real time, without any manual handoff
- Claims submission and denial follow-up — we submit claims directly and follow up on denials automatically so clinics stop leaving money on the table
- Payments and billing — automated reminders and collection

Our goal is to replace the $15,000/month stack clinics currently use with a single platform starting at $7,500/month.

📈 Traction

- $17K → $50K MRR in 8 weeks, 39% MoM growth
- $1.8M in incremental revenue driven for customers since September 2025
- 60+ clinics live across the US, Australia, and the UK
- Official voice provider for 2 major practice management platforms

🙏 Our ask

- Intros to dental groups, DSOs, or healthcare operators
- Feedback from founders who scaled vertical SaaS or voice-heavy products
- Anyone who has navigated insurance and claims workflows at scale

Happy to give any YC founder a live walkthrough.

Reach us at founders@patientdesk.ai or at patientdesk.ai

US-based healthtech startup Patientdesk.ai has secured $1 million in pre-seed funding in a round led by Y Combinator, with participation from E2VC.

Founded by Emre Kaplaner, Öncel Özgül, and Fikri Şan Köktaş, Patientdesk.ai is building voice AI-powered solutions to automate patient intake processes for healthcare clinics. The company plans to use the new funding to accelerate product development and expand its international integrations. As part of its growth roadmap, Patientdesk.ai is also preparing to open a Seed round in the near future.

Y Combinator is known for backing global technology leaders such as Airbnb, Uber, and Stripe at early stages — making its support a notable milestone for the startup.

Patientdesk.ai focuses primarily on dental clinics and other healthcare providers, offering an end-to-end voice AI system that automates:

- Incoming call responses
- Appointment scheduling
- Patient data collection
- Automatic transfer of patient information into clinic management systems

By digitizing and automating these processes, the company aims to reduce administrative burden while improving operational efficiency for clinics.

### Strong US Market Positioning

Patientdesk.ai integrates directly with widely used clinic management software platforms across the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom. Notably, the startup offers a real-time insurance verification capability during calls in the US market — a feature that strengthens its competitive positioning.

Currently working with more than 60 clinics, the US-based startup is actively expanding through strategic partnerships. In this context, Patientdesk.ai is collaborating with CorePractice, one of the popular clinic management systems in its segment.

The company also confirmed that it has established strategic partnerships with two major global healthtech firms, although the names of these partners remain undisclosed for now.

With voice AI increasingly transforming healthcare operations, Patientdesk.ai is positioning itself as a scalable infrastructure layer for next-generation clinic automation.

# Patientdesk AI Raises $1M Pre-Seed Backed by Y Combinator to Modernize Dental Front Desks

YC-backed Patientdesk AI expands patient-aware voice AI that verifies insurance in real time and automates dental front desk operations across 60+ clinics.

Patientdesk was built to handle real dental workflows, not just book appointments. Real-time insurance verification and patient awareness are what make the difference.”

— Oncel Ozgul, Co-Founder & CEO of Patientdesk AI

SAN FRANCISCO, CA, UNITED STATES, February 19, 2026 / EINPresswire.com/ — Patientdesk AI, a Y Combinator-backed startup building patient-aware AI for dental clinics, announced it has raised a $1 million pre-seed round led by Y Combinator and E2VC.

Patientdesk AI is building an AI-powered front desk system designed specifically for dental practices. Unlike generic AI booking tools, Patientdesk handles the full patient intake flow, including answering inbound calls, qualifying patients, booking appointments, verifying insurance in real time during the call, and managing payments and deposits.

Dental practices often lose patients before they ever book due to missed calls, delayed insurance checks, and manual front desk workflows. Patientdesk was built to address these operational gaps by acting as a patient-aware AI receptionist that understands both the clinic and the patient context.

The platform integrates directly with major dental practice management systems and adapts to how each clinic operates. Before going live, Patientdesk runs an AI audit inside the clinic’s systems to understand scheduling rules, treatment workflows, and how patient data is structured. This allows the AI to handle real-world dental workflows rather than relying on generic scripts.

Patientdesk AI is currently live in more than 60 dental clinics across the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom. In December, one clinic generated over $350,000 in revenue directly from Patientdesk-managed bookings.

A key differentiator of Patientdesk is real-time insurance verification during live patient calls. While most booking tools collect insurance information and require follow-up callbacks, Patientdesk verifies coverage instantly and explains benefits during the call. This reduces patient hesitation and increases confirmed bookings for high-value treatments.

The company plans to use the new funding to expand insurance verification capabilities, deepen integrations with dental practice management systems, and scale deployments across larger dental groups and DSOs.

Patientdesk AI was founded by Oncel Ozgul, San Koktas, and Emre Kaplaner, a team with experience building AI systems for healthcare and high-volume operational environments. The company is part of the Y Combinator W26 batch.

More information is available at https://www.patientdesk.ai.

# Patientdesk AI

 United States · Health · Latest deal Feb 23 · raised $1M 

#### Summary

Patientdesk AI, a San Francisco-based company, raised $1 million in pre-seed funding led by Y Combinator and E2VC. The funding will enhance insurance verification capabilities, improve integrations with dental practice management systems, and scale deployments across larger dental groups and DSOs.

#### What it does

Patientdesk AI is developing a platform that streamlines insurance verification processes specifically for dental practices. By integrating with existing dental practice management systems, it aims to reduce administrative burdens and improve operational efficiency for dental service organizations (DSOs).

#### Traction

The company is targeting larger dental groups and DSOs, indicating a focus on a significant segment of the healthcare market that often struggles with insurance verification complexities. The pre-seed funding suggests early-stage validation and interest from notable investors.

#### Trend impact

Patientdesk AI is poised to disrupt the traditional, cumbersome insurance verification workflows that have long plagued dental practices, potentially challenging established players in the dental tech space. By leveraging automation and integration, it addresses a critical pain point in the dental industry, which is increasingly reliant on technology to enhance patient care and operational efficiency.
